title: Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals for Industry
summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving industry professionals and their advisers a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks and controls that matter.
intro: This training programme equips people working in and around the crypto-asset industry with a working understanding of blockchain technology and the crypto-asset ecosystem, and the practical tools to build, run, advise and invest in digital asset businesses responsibly.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give industry professionals a comprehensive, practical grounding in how blockchain technology works and how crypto-asset markets, products and service providers operate. Participants leave able to analyse business models and their economic function, identify the key prudential, conduct and financial crime risks, and build the governance and controls that clients, investors, banking partners and supervisors expect.
sections.What It Covers: Blockchain technology, crypto-asset typology and market structure, wallets and custody, crypto-asset service provider business models, tokenisation, stablecoins and unbacked crypto-assets, DeFi and emerging technologies, enterprise risk, financial crime and the travel rule, and the strategic and regulatory outlook for digital finance.
Intended Audience: Founders, senior managers and staff of crypto-asset service providers, issuers and fintech firms, and of banks, asset managers and payment firms entering digital assets
Compliance, risk, MLRO, legal, operations and product professionals working on digital asset activities
Consultants, lawyers, auditors, investors and other advisers who support crypto-asset businesses
Learning Objectives: Explain how blockchain and distributed ledger technology operate within digital finance
Analyse crypto-asset types and business models to determine their economic function, revenue drivers and risk profile
Evaluate the risks of custody, tokenisation and stablecoins and the controls that manage them
Design the activities, governance and controls of a credible crypto-asset service provider
Apply AML/CFT requirements, including the travel rule, to crypto-asset operations
Evaluate emerging trends and regulatory developments and position the business to adapt and grow
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about four hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines technical explanation with case studies, red flags and practical control exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored to the business model and markets of the participants.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial services, compliance, risk or advisory work is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
Basel Committee, Prudential Treatment of Cryptoasset Exposures (2022)

modules.title: Foundations of Blockchain Technology
modules.summary: An introduction to how blockchains record and validate transactions, and the advantages, trade-offs and limitations of decentralised ledgers compared with centralised databases.
objectives: Explain how blockchain technology operates in practice
Analyse consensus mechanisms and their implications
Evaluate technological limitations and scalability challenges
syllabus: Distributed ledgers: how data is recorded and validated across networks
Blocks, hashing and immutability: how cryptography protects integrity
Proof of work, proof of stake and other consensus mechanisms
Public, private and permissioned networks: use cases and limits

modules.title: Crypto-Assets and Market Structure
modules.summary: The typology of crypto-assets and the structure of crypto markets, following the money to understand how value is created, transferred and traded across centralised and decentralised platforms.
objectives: Classify the main types of crypto-asset
Analyse market structures, incentives and trading dynamics
Evaluate risks associated with different market participants
syllabus: Cryptocurrencies, utility, governance and security tokens
Exchanges, brokers, market makers and institutional participants
Centralised exchanges versus decentralised trading platforms
Liquidity, price formation and market fragmentation risks

modules.title: Wallets, Custody and Key Management
modules.summary: How control of crypto-assets rests on cryptographic keys, the custody models firms use to safeguard client assets, and the operational and governance controls clients, auditors and supervisors will test.
objectives: Explain how private keys determine control of assets
Evaluate custody models and their risks
Assess operational and cyber risks in custody arrangements
syllabus: Public and private keys: how asset control works
Hot, cold, hardware, multi-signature and custodial wallets
Segregation, reconciliation and safeguarding of client assets
Key loss, hacks and system failure: lessons from custody incidents

modules.title: Crypto-Asset Service Providers and Business Models
modules.summary: The roles, activities and business models of crypto-asset service providers, how they make money, and how to determine which licences and registrations a business needs.
objectives: Identify core service provider activities and services
Analyse business models, revenue sources and unit economics in crypto markets
Determine the perimeter, licensing and registration needs of a business
syllabus: Exchanges, brokers and trading platforms: operating structures
Custodians, wallet providers, issuers and token platforms
Infrastructure providers supporting crypto-asset markets
Hybrid and decentralised models: perimeter and licensing implications

modules.title: Tokenisation
modules.summary: How traditional financial assets are represented on distributed ledgers, the legal, operational and technological considerations involved, and the opportunities and risks for firms as market structure evolves.
objectives: Explain the main tokenisation models
Analyse tokenised asset and fund structures
Evaluate the legal and operational risks of tokenisation
syllabus: Tokenising real-world assets: equities, bonds and funds
Smart contracts governing asset behaviour and transfer restrictions
Claimed benefits: efficiency, transparency and liquidity
Legal enforceability, settlement finality and custody risks

modules.title: Stablecoins and Unbacked Crypto-Assets
modules.summary: The design, uses and risks of stablecoins compared with unbacked crypto-assets, with a focus on reserves, redemption and the conditions under which a peg can fail.
objectives: Classify stablecoin types and distinguish them from unbacked crypto-assets
Evaluate reserve, liquidity and redemption risks
Assess governance, disclosure and oversight requirements
syllabus: Fiat-backed, crypto-collateralised and algorithmic stablecoins
Use cases in payments, trading and settlement
Reserve composition, redemption mechanics and stress scenarios
De-pegging, governance failures and transparency red flags

modules.title: DeFi and Emerging Financial Technologies
modules.summary: The technologies reshaping digital finance, including smart contracts, decentralised finance, interoperability and digital identity, and what they mean for firms' products, risks and strategy.
objectives: Explain smart contracts and decentralised finance
Analyse interoperability and integration challenges
Evaluate the risks and opportunities of new technologies
syllabus: Smart contracts and automated transaction execution
DeFi protocols: lending, exchange and yield structures
Bridges, interoperability and cross-chain risk
Digital identity, on-chain credentials and AI in digital finance

modules.title: Managing Risk in a Crypto-Asset Business
modules.summary: A structured framework for identifying, assessing and controlling risks in a crypto-asset business, showing how market, operational, cyber and governance risks interact within firms and markets.
objectives: Identify the key risk categories in digital finance
Design operational, cyber and governance controls for a crypto firm
Manage market volatility, leverage and market abuse risks
syllabus: Market volatility, leverage and price dynamics
Operational failures, cyber threats and attack vectors
Governance and control failures: lessons from firm collapses
Market abuse and manipulation in crypto markets

modules.title: Financial Crime and AML/CFT Risks
modules.summary: Financial crime risks in crypto-asset markets and the application of AML/CFT frameworks, including blockchain analytics, privacy-enhancing technologies and the FATF travel rule.
objectives: Explain AML/CFT obligations for virtual asset service providers
Apply travel rule requirements and recognise implementation challenges
Evaluate transaction monitoring and blockchain analytics tools
syllabus: Illicit finance typologies in crypto-asset ecosystems
Blockchain tracing and analytics: capabilities and limits
Mixers, privacy coins and privacy-enhancing technologies
FATF Recommendation 15 and the travel rule in practice

modules.title: Digital Finance Strategy and the Regulatory Outlook
modules.summary: Brings the programme together to examine how tokenisation, stablecoins and DeFi are reshaping markets and regulation, and how firms can position themselves to grow while meeting rising expectations.
objectives: Explain the trends shaping the future of digital finance
Compare regulatory approaches and international standards across jurisdictions
Evaluate strategic options, licensing choices and readiness for regulatory change
syllabus: Comprehensive crypto-asset regimes, convergence and divergence across jurisdictions
International standards: FSB, IOSCO, FATF and the Basel Committee
Institutional adoption, stablecoins in payments and tokenised infrastructure
Workshop: a growth and regulatory readiness plan for a crypto-asset business

related.title: Digital Money and Tokenisation for Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping banks, payment firms, asset managers and infrastructures decide whether and how to participate in digital money and tokenisation.

related.title: Quantum and Cryptographic Resilience for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms understand the quantum threat, build a cryptographic inventory, plan post-quantum migration and report readiness to the board and supervisors.

related.title: Tokenisation of Financial Markets for Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme for firms designing, launching and running tokenised securities, funds and platforms, from business case and legal structure to custody, settlement and supervisory engagement.

related.title: FinTech Business Models: Understanding and Supervising Innovation
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and firm compliance teams to understand how FinTech business models make money, grow and fail, and to assess their risks.

related.title: Agentic AI and Autonomous Finance for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms deploy AI agents that act and transact with sound authority, controls, governance and customer protection.

related.title: AI Governance for Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving compliance, risk, model risk and technology staff the tools to design, run and evidence robust AI governance across the firm.
